title: feat: trajectory3d.js, a 3-D path with a time marker (zero-build)
body:
## What

`mountTrajectory3D(host, options)` draws a path through three dimensions on a plain 2-D canvas, with a marker at the current time and the last `trail` seconds drawn heavier. It returns `{update, setTime, show, resetView, destroy}`. Zero-build, no dependencies, same shape as `cellfield.js` (a `mount*` function plus a `.d.ts`).

- `trajectory3d.js` + `trajectory3d.d.ts` at the repo root
- `package.json`: shipped in `files`, new entry point `./trajectory3d.js`
- `dev_check.py`: `check_trajectory3d()`; `scripts/api_surface.py` tracks the export and the handle methods, so a later rename forces a breaking bump
- Story: **Science / 3-D views / Path with a time marker (zero-build, synthetic)**
- Docs: `INTEGRATION.md` § 5 (and the allow-list line in § 1), a row in `README.md`

## Versioning

**Additive, so a patch.** A new entry point and nothing existing changes. The React `Trajectory3D` (the hodogram on `Scene3D`) is a separate view and is untouched; no React wrapper was added for this module, to avoid a name collision.

## Public-repo rule

- **Method:** a 3-D state-space path / phase portrait with a playhead. Standard.
- **Data:** the story integrates the Lorenz system (Lorenz 1963) in the story itself. Synthetic, and labelled so.
- **Findings:** none shown or stated.

## Differences from the private copy it was ported from

- Axes are right-handed and positive pitch looks down, as in `src/science/space` (the original was left-handed, seen from below). Paths appear mirrored relative to the original.
- On a drag the near side follows the pointer (direction reversed).
- A two-finger touch pinch zooms. Before, only Ctrl/Cmd-scroll did.
- Arrow keys turn and `+`/`-` zoom when the canvas has focus.
- Redraws on a theme change; falls back to `--chart-1` / `--chart-4` on the React theme.

## Checked

- `python3 dev_check.py`: 429/429
- `npx tsc -p .`: clean
- `python3 scripts/api_surface.py --removed v0.5.16`: nothing removed
- In a browser: a zero-build page on `design.css` and the Storybook story, light and dark, and at 375 px (no sideways scroll). Turn, pinch, Ctrl-scroll zoom, keyboard, reset, destroy and live theme switch work; a plain scroll is left to the page. Pinch was tested with synthetic pointer events, not on a real phone.

## Note for consumers

The canvas takes every touch that starts on it (`touch-action: none`), so a page needs scroll room beside or below it on a phone. Documented in `INTEGRATION.md`.

title: Patents companion: the plan may ask patent-fetch what is already patented
body:
Adds a second companion tool, built the same way as `datasets`. It is off until enabled, and is asked only when the planner judges that the question is about a device, a method or another invention.

**A companion can now be a command**
- [patent-fetch](https://github.com/polarizetech/patent-fetch) ships a command line and no MCP server, and offers `patent-fetch --json search` for gateways.
- `upstream.Command` runs a configured command and reads its standard output as JSON.
- The command is started with an argument list, never through a shell, so a query a model wrote is always one argument.
- It reports a missing command or a timeout as `unavailable`, and a non-zero exit with the last line of stderr.
- `Companion.transport` (`mcp` or `command`) picks the client.

**The `patents` companion**
- Runs one search per planner query and merges hits by publication number.
- patent-fetch does not rank, so the hits are ordered by the paper library's `relevance` of each title to the question.
- Prints the services' own records under "Existing patents on this": number, year, applicants or inventors, classes, status in the service's words, and a link.
- Fetches nothing, and never becomes evidence for a claim.
- The section states that it is not a legal opinion and that finding none is not evidence that none exists.
- Limits name every service that had no account or did not answer. They also say when only Europe PMC's archive answered (life-science patents, none after 2012), so a search that could not see recent patents does not read as "none exist".

**Config** (`config/mcp-gateway.example.json`): `"patents": {"command": "patent-fetch", "args": ["--json"], "enabled": false}`.

**Tested:**
- 249 tests pass, and ruff and pyright are clean.
- New tests cover merging and ordering, each limits case, and the command transport: a shell-hostile query passed as one argument, a non-zero exit, non-JSON output, a timeout, and a command that is not installed.
- New tests also cover a full run that requests patents, and a run where the tool is missing and the run continues.
- A live check against the real command returned 16 records for two queries, listed six, and gave the correct limits.

title: Ask the caller to search the web when the library cannot
body:
## Summary

The last resort after the scholarly providers is a web search. Until now that needed a hosted SearXNG instance; without one, the fallback was skipped.

paper-fetch runs no language model, but its caller is usually a model with its own web search. This PR hands the last step to the caller, so nothing needs hosting.

- **`ask_the_web` in search results.** When the fallback is wanted (no open-access hit) and the library's own web search did not answer, the result carries `ask_the_web` with `why`, the `query`, what happened to the library's own web search, and `how` to proceed. "Did not answer" means `SEARXNG_URL` is unset or SearXNG is down.
- **`leads`**, available as `Library.leads`, the MCP `leads` tool and `paper-fetch leads <url> ...`. It takes the URLs the caller found. It reads a DOI, PMID, PMCID or arXiv id out of each, using the web provider's own parser, marks what is already held, and returns what to `fetch`. It makes no network calls. A URL with no identifier is returned under `no_identifier` rather than dropped.
- **MCP instructions** tell the model what to do when it sees `ask_the_web`.

The rule is unchanged: nothing is downloaded from a web page. An identifier goes through the open-access providers, which decide whether a copy may be kept.

SearXNG still works when configured, and then nothing is asked of the caller. `web_fallback=False` and `PAPER_FETCH_WEB_FALLBACK=0` turn off the request along with the fallback.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run pytest`: 375 passed, 96% coverage. New tests in `tests/test_fallbacks.py` cover:
  - `ask_the_web` when no web search is configured or SearXNG is down;
  - no `ask_the_web` when the fallback is off, not needed, or SearXNG answered;
  - `leads` parsing, de-duplication, held marking, and making no network call;
  - the CLI output and the MCP tool.
- [x] `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `pyright` are clean.
- [x] Live on this machine (no SearXNG): a no-hit search printed the ask-the-web prompt. `leads` on a DOI URL and a PubMed URL returned both identifiers marked as held, and returned a URL with no identifier under `no_identifier`.

title: Wait out a provider's outside problems; flag its defects
body:
## Summary

A search already asks every provider and merges whatever answers, with web search last. This PR fixes how a *failing* provider is treated, by telling two kinds of failure apart.

**An outside problem** means the service is down, rate-limiting us or out of allowance.
- The provider is reported as `unavailable` and the other providers answer.
- The provider is then left alone for a while instead of being asked again by every search:
  - 60 s after an outage
  - 300 s after a 429
  - an hour after OpenAlex's daily allowance
  - the rest of the process after scite's monthly one
- While paused it isn't called. Its report says `unavailable` with `paused: true` and the original reason.
- A cached answer is still served, and `refresh=True` asks anyway.

**A defect** means the service rejected our request or its answer changed shape. Waiting won't fix it, so:
- It is never paused.
- Its report says `error` with `broken: true`.
- The search result carries a top-level `broken` list.
- The CLI prints `! BROKEN: …` on stderr.
- The MCP server's instructions tell the model to tell the user.
- The traceback is logged to a local file, shown by `paper-fetch problems --trace`.

## The bug this fixes

Nine query helpers did `if r.status != 200: return []`. A provider answering 500, or rejecting a malformed query with 400, was reported as **`ok`, 0 hits**, so an outage or a bug read as "nothing in the literature".

They now go through `Provider._answered`, which raises one kind of failure or the other. It applies only to query endpoints, which answer 200 with an empty list when nothing matches. A lookup by identifier can still treat a 404 as "not known".

## Also in this PR

- **scite:** its failures are sorted the same way. A spent allowance or a busy service is unavailable. A rejected request, a JSON-RPC error, an unrecognised tool error or an answer without `hits` is a defect.
- **OpenAlex:** a 429 or 5xx is unavailable rather than a generic error.
- **Locating copies:** a defect met while locating a copy is logged too.
- **README install lines:** they used a PyPI name that doesn't exist (404). They now install from this repository.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run pytest`: 367 passed, 96% coverage. Five existing tests relied on a 404 meaning "empty" and now use real empty answers.
  - `tests/test_fallbacks.py` covers pausing, the pause lengths, cache served while paused, defects named and logged, and web search asked when every provider is down.
  - `tests/test_providers.py` checks that all eight query providers treat a 503 or 403 as unavailable and a 400 as broken.
  - `tests/test_scite.py` covers the scite classification.
- [x] `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `pyright` are clean.
- [x] Live: five searches in one process. All nine default providers answered `ok`, including for a nonsense query, so none had been failing silently. scite reported its spent allowance once and was reported as paused on the next search. Zero defects were logged.

title: Make scite opt-in: its subscription allows 250 calls a month
body:
## Summary

Makes **scite opt-in**. Its subscription allows 250 MCP calls a month, and one day in the default search set spent all of it.

After #7, every paper-fetch search asked scite, and a profile search asked it up to three times (once per query variant). With the research-rag gateway and about a dozen sessions searching, the month's allowance was gone within a day. scite now answers "You have reached your monthly MCP usage limit (250 calls)".

## What changes

- **Default set:** scite is no longer in `DEFAULT_SEARCH`. An ordinary search doesn't touch it.
- **Opting in:** a search asks scite on top of the usual providers with `also=["scite"]` in Python, `--scite` on the CLI, or `scite: true` on the MCP `search` tool. Naming it in `PAPER_FETCH_SEARCH_PROVIDERS` or `providers=` still works.
- **One call per search:** `Provider.metered` is new and is True for scite. A metered provider is asked the query as written, once, and never a profile's variants.
- **Session reuse:** the opted-in provider is built once per `Library`, so scite's MCP session is reused instead of opened per search. One thread uses that session at a time.
- **Docs:** README and `CLAUDE.md` record the limit and how to opt in.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run pytest`: 329 passed, 95% coverage. New tests cover:
  - scite is asked only when told to;
  - `also` doesn't ask a provider twice and reuses the session;
  - a metered provider is skipped for profile variants;
  - the CLI flag and the MCP parameter pass the opt-in through.
- [x] `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `pyright` are clean.
- [x] Live: a default `paper-fetch search` reports the nine usual providers and no scite.
- [x] Live: `--scite` asks scite by name. It currently returns scite's monthly-limit message, reported as `unavailable`.
- [ ] A successful live scite search through the opt-in path. This can't run until the allowance resets.

title: One Library, many threads: lock the catalogue, memory, collections and pacing
body:
Follow-up to #8. An MCP server runs every tool call on a worker thread, so one `Library` is used from several threads at once. #8 locked the passage index's connection. This PR covers the rest of the state those threads share.

- **Catalogue:**
  - One lock guards the in-memory dictionary and its save.
  - Readers that walk the catalogue take a snapshot (`_rows()`). Writers go through `_record` / `_forget`.
  - A save now updates the dictionary in place without emptying it. Before, a lookup from another thread mid-save could find a held paper missing and fetch it again.
  - `rebuild_index` builds the new catalogue aside and swaps it in whole.
- **Search memory and collections:** each read-modify-write holds a lock, so no thread's row or member is lost.
- **Lazily built parts** (profiles, memory, passage index, reranker): built once.
- **Provider request spacing:** two threads could both pass the wait at once and break a rate limit such as PLOS's 10 per minute. The wait is now taken under a per-provider lock.

No lock is held across a fetch or a search, so slow network work does not block other calls. The locks are per process; the cross-process behaviour is unchanged.

**Tested:**
- `tests/test_threads.py` runs each part from 16 threads. All five tests fail on main and pass here.
- The thread tests passed 25 runs in a row.
- All 324 tests pass, and ruff and pyright are clean.

title: Lock the passage index's connection: tool calls run on worker threads
body:
**What failed:** `retrieve` failed intermittently in service. The gateway log shows 13 failed calls. Eleven are `sqlite3.InterfaceError: bad parameter or other API misuse`, and one is passage text read back as undecodable bytes.

**Cause:** the MCP library runs every sync tool on a worker thread (`anyio.to_thread.run_sync`), so overlapping `retrieve` calls used the passage index's single SQLite connection at the same time. The index was written as if calls were serial.

**Fix:** `PassageIndex` holds an `RLock` around every use of its connection, including reads, writes and the cached vector matrix. Embedding, the slow part of indexing, stays outside the lock, so indexing a paper does not block retrieval for seconds.

**Tested:**
- A new test runs 200 mixed `search` / `passages` / `paper` / `stats` / `add` calls across 16 threads on one index. It fails on main and passes here.
- All 319 tests pass, and ruff and pyright are clean.

Not covered: `Library`'s other shared state (the in-memory catalogue) is also reached from several threads. No failure from it appears in the logs, so this PR leaves it alone.

title: Release v0.8.1: generated CI can install private dependencies
body:
## Why

A repo that pins the organisation's private repos by git URL in `pyproject.toml` fails at `uv sync` in GitHub Actions (`fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': terminal prompts disabled`), because the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` reads only its own repo. `make check` is then skipped, so the scaffold check never runs. This was worked around by hand in polarizetech/matched-entropy-demodulation#11.

## What

- **Templates** (study, sim, tool, workbench): the workflow reads an optional `PRIVATE_DEPS_TOKEN` secret and, when it is set, rewrites `https://github.com/{{org}}/` to use it. The org comes from the profile, not hard-coded.
- **Install step**: always runs `uv sync --frozen || uv sync`. A failure becomes a `::warning::` only when the token is unset and `pyproject.toml` or `uv.lock` mentions `github.com/<org>/`; any other failed install still fails the job.
- **Docs**: the secret is described in PROTOCOL.md § 4; UPGRADING.md and CHANGELOG.md have their v0.8.1 sections.
- **Version**: 0.8.1 in `bin/scaffold`, `CITATION.cff` and both `plugin.json` files.

## Difference from the hand fix

matched-entropy-demodulation#11 skips `uv sync` whenever the token is unset. This does not, so a repo with only public dependencies and no secret keeps installing as before.

## Upgrading from v0.8.0

- An unedited v0.8.0 workflow is replaced by `scaffold update` (by lock hash, or without a lock by matching what v0.8.0 wrote, which needs the scaffold's git history and tag).
- An edited workflow keeps its edits and only the `ref:` moves; `--adopt .github/workflows/check.yml` replaces it.

## Tests

`python3 -m unittest discover tests`: 67 run, 1 skipped (needs Python 3.11+), all pass locally. New tests cover the rendered org per profile, the install step's three outcomes with a stand-in `uv`, and the v0.8.0 upgrade with and without a lock. One existing test changed: it asserted no `{{` anywhere in a new repo, which `${{ secrets.… }}` trips; it now looks for unfilled `{{placeholder}}` patterns.

The generated workflow has not yet run in GitHub Actions.

## Not in this PR

Tagging `v0.8.1` after merge. With private pins and no secret, `make check` still fails afterwards in a repo that has `tests/`, since `uv run pytest` needs the dependencies.

title: Add scite as a search provider, through its MCP server
body:
## Summary

Adds **scite** as a search provider alongside OpenAlex and the others. It uses your scite subscription and needs no API key.

scite's REST search (`/api_partner/search`) returns 401 without a partner token, which comes from their sales team. Its MCP server (`https://api.scite.ai/mcp`) accepts the subscriber's own sign-in instead: OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and PKCE. So the provider is a small MCP client written against `Http`. It sends `initialize`, then `tools/call search_literature`.

## What changes

- **Sign-in:** `paper-fetch scite-login` opens the browser once and stores the sign-in in `~/.config/paper-fetch/scite-oauth.json` (mode 0600). It is never written to the shared store. `scite-logout` removes it.
- **Token renewal:** the access token is renewed automatically. scite rotates the refresh token on every use, so the file is re-read before a refresh and once more after a refused one.
- **Provider:** `providers/scite.py` is search-only, like `doaj`. It is in the default search set and reported `skipped` until someone signs in. Its results are not cached.
- **What a hit keeps:** DOI, title, year, three authors, scite's open-access flag and status, the citation tally and editorial notices.
- **What a hit drops:** scite's access links (they carry the account's email address), abstracts and citation statements.
- **Merged search results:** a hit that scite found carries a `scite` key with the tally, `oa_status` and `editorial_notices`.
- **HTTP layer:** `Http.post` is new. It returns a 4xx response as an answer, the way `get` does. `http.py` stays the only module that calls `urlopen`.
- **Docs:** README, `CLAUDE.md` and `INTEGRATION.md` are updated.

## Design notes

- **No `mcp` SDK in the core.** The core stays standard-library plus pypdf, and all outbound requests still go through `Http`. The one new socket is the loopback listener that receives the browser redirect during login.
- **`oa_only`:** the tool has no open-access filter. The provider asks for three times `limit` (capped at 50, because every hit carries a citation list) and drops what scite marks closed.
- **Failures:** an expired sign-in, a 429, a tool error or an unreachable server is reported as `unavailable` with what to do, never as zero results.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run pytest`: 318 passed, 95% coverage (29 new tests in `tests/test_scite.py`, against a fake scite server).
- [x] `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `pyright` are clean.
- [x] Live sign-in through the browser on 2026-10-05; the stored file is mode 0600.
- [x] Live search: 5 hits in 3.7 s (3 POSTs on a new session), with nothing from the access links kept.
- [x] Live `oa_only` search: every hit returned is open.
- [x] Live token refresh: forced by expiring the token locally. The access token changed and the refresh token rotated.
- [x] Live federated search: `paper-fetch search … --providers scite,openalex,europepmc` merged hits across the three providers.

title: Datasets companion: one call to dataset-fetch's recommend
body:
dataset-fetch now has `recommend(topic)` (polarizetech/dataset-fetch#12). Choosing catalogues, phrasing queries and ranking datasets now live there, the way paper search lives in paper-fetch. This switches the `datasets` companion to that one call.

- **Calls:** one `recommend` call per planner query, at most two.
- **Merging:** cards are merged by reference, keeping the better score. Records with verified data files come first, then each by dataset-fetch's own score.
- **Printing:** the answer shows the tool's own fields: catalogue and kind, licence, files, subjects, modalities, creators, DOI, a pinned reference, and the tool's reason for listing it. Records that hold only documents, and lower-ranked records, are counted rather than listed.
- **Failures:** a query that `recommend` refuses doesn't discard the other query's results. A catalogue that was silent on every query is named in Limits.
- **Removed:** the companion's own loop over catalogues, the Zenodo query rewrite, the card reading and the document filter.

**Tested:**
- 238 tests pass, and ruff and pyright are clean.
- **Live:** one query, about 19 s.

  - Every listed record held data, including PhysioNet blood-pressure databases and a structured-exercise dataset.

title: Fix spectrum(): summarise every bin in each display bucket
body:
## The bug

`quality.spectrum()` promised to summarise Goertzel bins into display buckets, but evaluated only every `step`-th DFT bin and skipped the rest. On a record longer than a couple of seconds a narrow line fell between the evaluated bins and disappeared. A 260-count 10 Hz sine in noise over 20 s drew its tallest point at 35.65 Hz, about 1.7 counts. The Monitor tab's spectrum (`POST /spectrum`, up to 20 s every ~500 ms) was affected the same way.

## The fix

- Every transform bin in the range is evaluated, and each bucket reports the **maximum** amplitude of the bins it covers. A maximum keeps a narrow line at its own amplitude however long the record is; a mean of power would dilute it. The price, stated in the docstring: the noise floor of the display rises slowly with record length, and it is not a power density.
- Cost: one stdlib radix-2 FFT of the Hann-windowed record, zero-padded to the next power of two at or above twice its length, over at most the most recent 16,384 samples (65 s at 250 Hz). The padding bounds the scalloping loss at 4 %.
- `freqs` are now bucket centres. `resolution_hz` keeps its meaning (rate / samples used). New fields: `bucket_hz`, `bin_hz`, `samples_used`, `summary`. The web client needs no change.

| Record | Tallest point | Amplitude (input 260) | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 s | 10.01 Hz | 259.5 | 3 ms |
| 20 s | 9.97 Hz | 256.8 | 56 ms |
| 60 s | 9.98 Hz | 257.0 | 119 ms |

## Checks

- `apps/server/dev_check.py`: a 10 Hz sine in noise at 2 s, 20 s and 60 s must be the tallest point, within one bucket of 10 Hz and within 10 % of the input amplitude; plus a check on the sample cap.
- `python3 scripts/check.py`: all seven suites pass. `check_docs.py` run against the blog post: in step. ruff clean.

## Versioning

No version bump and no `model-v*` tag. `quality.py` is in the measuring chain, but `spectrum()` feeds only the drawing: nothing it returns is stored in a session or an export, and `assess()` and `bands()` are unchanged. The CHANGELOG entry says so. If this should be 0.2.1 instead, that is a follow-up commit here.

title: Docs site, generated by automatic-documentation-site
body:
## What this adds

A generated docs site for this repository, built by [automatic-documentation-site](https://github.com/polarizetech/automatic-documentation-site). Nothing on it is written by hand: a page is fixed by fixing the Markdown file, docstring or story it names.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `docs-site.toml` | what the site is generated from |
| `docs-site/stories/` | four stories: real calls run at build time |
| `.github/workflows/docs-site.yml` | rebuilds on every push to `main` and deploys to GitHub Pages |
| `docs-site/README.md` | how to build and read it locally |
| `.gitignore` | the build output and story cache |

No code under `apps/` changes.

## What the site contains (22 pages)

- **Guides:** the README (with Safety and the board photos), then the hardware, recording, standards, versioning, bridge, workbench and project documents.
- **API reference:** `apps/server` and `apps/web` Python, and the exported browser modules. 85 public symbols, read without importing or running anything.
- **Stories**, on synthetic or modelled inputs only, never a recording of a person:
  - what the front end can carry (`rig.carries`): alpha reachable, brainstem responses unreachable
  - which readouts fit in its band (`readouts.gate`)
  - the pre-flight verdict on a good, a flat and a railed channel (`quality.assess`)
  - the delivered sample rate (`timebase.RateEstimator` recovers a simulated 248.3 Hz)

## One story records a check that does not hold

`quality.spectrum` of a clean 10 Hz sine has no peak at 10 Hz on a 20 s record. Its docstring says it averages Goertzel bins into display buckets; the code evaluates every `step`-th bin, so a narrow line between them is missed. The story shows the check as it came out ("absent") and was not adjusted to pass. The fix belongs in a separate change.

## Checked

- `docsite build . --refresh --strict --publish pages` with the released tool (v0.2.1) and polarize-ui v0.5.15: 22 pages, 4/4 stories run.
- `python3 scripts/check.py`: every suite passes.
- The built site opens from a folder (`file://`) with plots, search and badges working.

## After merging

The workflow runs on `main` and deploys to https://polarizetech.github.io/olimex-shield/ (GitHub Pages is enabled, source: GitHub Actions).

Based on `main`. The extension catalogue on the `tool-only` work is not on `main` yet; when it lands it is one `[catalogue]` block in `docs-site.toml`.

title: Do not index reference lists that have no heading paragraph
body:
Found in a live run of retrieval-augmented-generation: a bibliography entry from a PDF was retrieved as a passage. The chunker only cut at a paragraph that was exactly "References". PDF text often has the heading on a line inside a paragraph, or loses it altogether.

**Detection** (`references_start`)
- A heading on a line of its own ("References", "6. References", "Literature Cited"), past the first third of the text.
- Or, with no heading: a run of at least 8 consecutively numbered entries starting at 1 that begins in the second half of the text, reaches its last tenth, and mostly carries publication years.
- Numbered lists in the body are kept. That covers lists that are short, early, have no years, or do not start at 1.

**Measured on 80 held papers:** 11 of 12 PDFs are now cut (none were before), every cut I read lands at the start of the list, and the 68 JATS and TEI texts are unaffected. An unnumbered author-year list with no heading is still not recognised.

**Existing indexes**
- The chunker has a version (`CHUNKER = 2`), kept in a new `chunked` table next to the `indexed_at` of the row it describes.
- The `papers` table is unchanged, so servers still running older code and sharing the file keep working. A paper one of them re-indexes counts as stale again.
- `has()` is false for a stale paper, so it is re-chunked the next time it is indexed. Passages whose text did not change keep their vectors, so only new text is embedded.
- `status` reports `stale`.

**Tested:** 287 tests pass, including the detector's positive and negative cases, vector reuse, an index from before versions existed, and a row rewritten by older code. ruff and pyright are clean.

title: Accept the library's own work ids; skip bad records when indexing and collecting
body:
## Problems
1. Works the library creates itself (\`pmcid-PMC5519140\`, \`doi-10.1214%2F12-aoas565supp\`) were rejected by \`index\`, \`collect\` and the MCP \`index\`/\`collect\` tools with "unrecognised identifier". One bad id also failed a whole batch.
2. \`paper-fetch index\` with no arguments aborted on the first unparseable record, leaving later works unindexed.

## Changes
- \`ids.normalize\` parses \`doi-\`/\`pmcid-\`/\`pmid-\`/\`arxiv-\` work ids, including percent-encoded DOIs. Behaviour for ordinary DOI / OpenAlex / PMID / PMCID inputs is unchanged and junk is still refused.
- \`index_works\` reads text from the catalogue row (no re-parse) and skips and reports unreadable records under \`skipped\`; the CLI prints each with its reason and a count.
- \`collect\` returns a \`rejected\` list instead of failing the batch.
- When OpenAlex has no record, \`fetch\` fills title, year, authors and DOI from Europe PMC (never fatal).
- Existing library records are not rewritten; already-stored metadata-less works are only enriched on a new \`fetch\`.

## Tests
\`tests/test_own_work_ids.py\`: 12 of its 19 cases fail on main and all pass here; full suite 278 passed, ruff and pyright clean.

title: Library reranking, per-item failures, fetch and quote fixes, companion tools
body:
Four changes that came out of live runs, plus the first companion tool.

**One model call with no answer costs that item, not the run** (follow-up to #3)
- Reading a passage: it is dropped with the flag `no_answer_from_model` and counted in Limits.
- Classifying a paper: it is graded `unclear` for this run, and that is not cached.
- Planning, synthesis and critique still end the run, as does an unreachable model.

**Reranking is the paper library's**
- The local-model reranker is removed. In a live run the 4B model spent 4.9 of 5.7 hours reranking.
- The library's cross-encoder (`PAPER_FETCH_RERANK_MODEL`) ranks passages. The pipeline keeps that order and only caps passages per paper and per sub-question.
- Without the setting, passages are read in retrieval order, and the run notes say so.

**Two bugs from that run**
- Fetch ordering now puts papers reported as open access first and papers reported as closed last. All six fetches had gone to closed papers.
- An exact quote match that stops inside a word or number is widened to the whole token. A stored quote read "5." where the passage said "5.9 mmHg".

**Companion tools** (`research_pipeline/companions.py`)
- With a companion configured under `companions` in the gateway config, the plan's schema gains a `tools` field restricted to the configured keys.
- Code calls each requested tool once, within set bounds, and prints the tool's own records in the answer. No model writes that section, and it never becomes evidence.
- A companion that fails is reported and the run goes on. Offline runs call none.
- First companion: `datasets`, which speaks dataset-fetch's MCP contract.
  - It searches every catalogue that takes a free-text query, with Zenodo restricted to dataset-typed records.
  - It reads the data cards, and counts documents-only records instead of listing them.
  - It orders the rest by the library's `relevance`.
- Adding another companion is one registry entry.

**Also**
- A generic `Upstream` MCP client; `PaperLibrary` is now one use of it.
- The design doc notes the planned "own endpoint" backend for private runs.

**Tested:**
- 237 tests pass. ruff and pyright are clean.
- Live against the real services: the library reranker returned on-topic passages, and the dataset companion searched three catalogues and read ten cards in 14 s.

title: A verifier call with no answer fails that check, not the run
body:
Found by a live run. One verify call generated 16,000 tokens without ever closing its JSON answer, hit the 600 s wall-clock limit, and ended the whole run. It happened twice.

- **Output cap:** every structured call is capped by `PIPELINE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` (default 2048), so a runaway call stops in about a minute.
- **Narrower error:** `ModelOutputError`, a subclass of `LLMError`, marks one failed call: out of time or tokens, or not JSON. An unreachable server or a client that stopped answering still raises `LLMError` and ends the run.
- **Failed checks:** a verifier call that fails this way is recorded as `CHECK_FAILED` and never counts as support.
- **Unverified claims:** a claim that no verifier answered for gets `VERIFIER_FAILED`. It is removed from the answer and counted in Limits. A real verdict from another check still decides the claim.

**Tested:**
- 230 tests pass, including tests for each case. ruff and pyright are clean.
- The live re-run completed. The two runaway checks were capped and reported in Limits, and the answer was produced.

title: Hand searching and indexing to paper-fetch
body:
Phase 3 of splitting the work between the two repositories. [paper-fetch](https://github.com/polarizetech/paper-fetch) now owns everything about finding and indexing papers (polarizetech/paper-fetch#2, #3, #4). This repository tells it the field and the concepts, then does everything after a passage is found: reading it, judging it, and checking the claims made from it.

**Changes**
- **Search:** `search` takes the domain's discipline profile (paper-fetch's profile with the same slug) and an optional collection (`--collection`, `PIPELINE_COLLECTION`, or `research_start(collection=)`). Searches are remembered, and the run log lists earlier searches on the same concept.
- **Planning:** the planner reads the profile's indexed terms, measures and search guidance. If the library has no such profile, the run says so.
- **Fetching:** the library's `relevance()` decides the fetch order, and the library indexes the fetched texts.
- **Retrieval:** passages come from the library's `retrieve()`, with stable ids (`<work>#p<ord>`) and the paper's metadata. `Evidence.passage_id` is now that string id.
- **Removed:** `index.py`, the embedding calls, the ONNX reranker, and the numpy dependency. The local-model reranker stays. Study-design notes move to `notes.sqlite`, keyed by the text hash.
- **Domains:** each keeps its evidence half (taxonomy, measures, critique rules, prompt rules). Anchors, sources and search guidance are now paper-fetch profiles, and `DomainPolicy.profile` names the profile to use. The domain template ships a `profile.toml`, and `DOMAINS.md` explains both halves.
- **Gateway:** the `rag__` tools read and index through the paper library's MCP session. Evidence ids keep the same format.

**Tests**
- 225 tests pass, and ruff and pyright are clean.
- The tests run against a real in-memory paper-fetch `Library`. It's a test-only dependency, pinned to a commit that is now on paper-fetch's main.
- The gateway tests run paper-fetch's real MCP server as the upstream, with every proxy pointed at a closed port so nothing can reach the network.
- New tests check that the profile reaches the planner, that profile and collection reach search, fetch and retrieval, and that a missing profile is noted.

**Live migration (already done locally)**
- The old index (735 papers, 33,852 passages, bge-m3 vectors) was copied into paper-fetch's index without re-embedding. Re-splitting six sampled texts reproduced their passages exactly, and the text hashes matched.
- The 272 cached study-design notes were copied into `notes.sqlite`.
- A round trip through the real gateway worked: hybrid retrieval, then a passing citation check.

title: Passage index and retrieval
body:
Phase 2 of moving paper searching and indexing into paper-fetch. This PR is stacked on #2 (the base is `search-profiles-collections`), so merge #2 first.

**What moves here from retrieval-augmented-generation**
- The passage index (`passages.py`). It is a local SQLite file built from held full texts, with FTS5 (BM25) always and dense vectors when `PAPER_FETCH_EMBED_MODEL` is set, fused by reciprocal rank.
- Chunking and hidden-character cleaning are unchanged, so passage offsets and `text_sha256` mean what they did in the RAG index. The paper row now also records how many hidden characters were removed (`hidden_chars`).
- Passage ids have the form `<work>#p<ord>` and survive rebuilds. `sha` identifies the passage text.
- The ONNX cross-encoder reranker (`rerank.py`), set with `PAPER_FETCH_RERANK_MODEL`.
- The embedder and the reranker are both deterministic: they return vectors and scores, never text. The model-based reranker and the prompt-injection scan stay in the application, because both concern a model reading the text.

**API**
- `Library.retrieve(queries, identifiers=, collection=, limit, per_paper, rerank)` indexes its scope on demand before retrieving.
- Also `index_works`, `paper_passages`, and the `passages` / `reranker` properties.
- New MCP tools: `retrieve`, `passages`, `index`. New CLI commands: `paper-fetch index [--rebuild]` and `paper-fetch retrieve`.
- New optional extras: `retrieval` (numpy) and `rerank` (onnxruntime, tokenizers, huggingface_hub). The core still depends only on pypdf and fonttools.
- Embedding requests go through the new `Http.post_json`, so the "only `http.py` and the store open URLs" guarantee still holds.

**Tested:**
- 257 tests pass offline: exact offsets, stable ids across rebuilds, hybrid and lexical ranking, scope, the per-paper cap, reranking, refusing a different embedding model, and the MCP and CLI commands. ruff and pyright are clean.
- A live run with bge-m3 against the real library, writing the index to a scratch file, turned 15 held papers into 1,405 passages in 94 s. A repeat query took about 10 ms.

**Next (phase 3):** retrieval-augmented-generation drops its own index and reranker and calls these tools, and its domains keep only their evidence rules.

title: Discipline profiles, named collections and search memory
body:
Phase 1 of moving paper searching and indexing out of retrieval-augmented-generation and into paper-fetch. Nothing here uses a language model: everything is string matching and bookkeeping, so it is repeatable and tested offline.

**Discipline profiles** (`profiles.py`, data in `profile_data/*.toml`)
- A profile holds the search half of a field: controlled terms (MeSH ids are validated), synonyms, measures, sources, and search guidance for whoever writes the queries.
- `search(profile=)` also runs up to two variants that swap a synonym for its indexed term ("HRV" → "heart rate variability"). It never swaps the other way. Hits whose titles name the field's terms rank first (`profile_match`), and results are merged across variants (`found_by`).
- Four profiles ship built in. They were converted from the RAG repo's domains. They don't narrow the provider set, because that would drop the repository providers that find open copies.
- A TOML file in `~/.config/paper-fetch/profiles/` adds a profile or replaces a built-in one by slug.

**Named collections** (`collection.py`)
- `papers/collections/<name>.json` holds a member list and a default profile. A paper is stored once, whichever collections list it.
- `fetch(collection=)` lists the paper in the collection. `collect` and `uncollect` add or remove members by any identifier.

**Search memory** (`memory.py`)
- `papers/memory/searches.jsonl` gets one row per search, written with the same re-read-and-append approach as the catalogue.
- Every search reports up to three earlier searches on the same concept, and marks each hit that an earlier search already found (`seen_before`).
- `recall` looks up past searches by concept, profile, collection or paper. A concept is the set of content words with synonyms mapped to indexed terms.

**Surfaces**
- New MCP tools: `profiles`, `recall`, `collections`, `collection`, `create_collection`, `collect`, `uncollect`. `search` and `fetch` take `profile` and `collection`.
- New CLI commands: `profiles`, `collection`, `collect`, `recall`, plus `--profile` and `--collection` on `search` and `fetch`.

**Tested:**
- 239 tests pass offline, including concurrent writers to the memory and to a collection. ruff and pyright are clean.
- A live search with the cardiovascular profile, run on an in-memory store, found the "heart rate variability" variant hits, ranked them first, and recalled the earlier "HRV" search at a score of 0.8.

**Next:**
- Phase 2: the passage index and retrieval move here.
- Phase 3: retrieval-augmented-generation calls paper-fetch for search, memory and retrieval, and its domains keep only the evidence half.
